explanation: String.format("%.2f", price) uses the JVM's default Locale when none is specified. On systems whose default locale uses a comma as the decimal separator (e.g. German, Turkish locales), this produces "12,50" instead of "12.50". Any downstream code expecting a period-separated decimal — parsing, JSON serialization, external APIs — breaks silently in those locales even though the same code works fine when tested under an English locale. The fix is to pass an explicit locale, e.g. String.format(Locale.US, "%.2f", price).
prompt: Is this price formatter safe to run on servers in any locale?
